claims.text: Superconductivity in the proposed uncharacterized high-entropy alloy is governed by the degree of local lattice distortion.
Atomic-size mismatch and chemical heterogeneity induce local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion modulates electron-phonon coupling relevant to superconducting pairing.
The starting material contains at least five metallic elements, each at no less than 5 at.%.
The starting material is a chemically disordered, largely single-phase FCC solid solution.
The starting FCC material has minimal lattice distortion.
Al is a larger-atomic-radius addition relative to the other unspecified constituents of the alloy.
Incremental Al additions increase local lattice distortion.
Increasing Al concentration can transform a single FCC high-entropy alloy into an FCC/BCC mixed-phase material.

Using identical powder-metallurgy and pressureless-sintering procedures across samples controls densification and diffusion history sufficiently to attribute superconducting changes mainly to composition.
Lattice strain and FCC/BCC phase coexistence alter the local electronic environment.
Enhanced lattice distortion localizes vibrational modes and alters the density of states near the Fermi level.
The distortion-induced vibrational and electronic changes increase electron-phonon coupling and strengthen superconducting pairing.
Excessive disorder or intermetallic-compound formation can disrupt superconductivity.
Increasing Al concentration can cause precipitation of intermetallic compounds, including FeNi, Al3Ni, CrNiFe, TiAl, and Ti3Al.
A moderate increase in controlled lattice distortion will raise Tc relative to the baseline alloy.
Excessive distortion or secondary-phase formation will produce no further Tc improvement or will reduce superconducting performance relative to the optimum.
The proposed relationship is restricted to alloys remaining largely homogeneous solid solutions or having only limited mixed-phase coexistence without extensive intermetallic precipitation.
XRD and TEM measurements of strain and phase content can be compared with resistance- and susceptibility-derived Tc across an Al-composition series.
Failure to observe either a systematic Tc change or an intermediate Tc optimum as measured distortion increases would falsify the hypothesis.
